checks: Check CPU trend for the last 30 minutes (is it rising, flat, or a spike?)
Check request rate and error rate over the same window
Check whether a deployment or config change landed in the last hour
Check pod/node CPU limits and requests for the affected service
Check downstream latency and dependency health
runbooks.description: Sustained high CPU on a service in production. Check whether it is real load, a bad deploy, or a runaway process before scaling.
runbooks.escalate_if: CPU stays above 90% after scaling, or error rate rises, or a second service is affected.
runbooks.name: High CPU on a service
runbooks.rollback: Scale back to the previous replica count and note the time of the change in the incident log.

checks: Read the pod logs for the last 3 restarts
Check the pod exit code and last termination reason (OOMKilled, Error, etc.)
Check recent image, config and secret changes for this service
Check memory requests and limits against actual usage
Check whether the pod can reach its database and other dependencies
runbooks.description: A pod keeps crashing and restarting. Do not keep restarting it blindly — find out why it is crashing first.
runbooks.escalate_if: The pod still crashes after a rollback, or the crash is caused by a database or shared dependency.
runbooks.name: Pod in CrashLoopBackOff
runbooks.rollback: Roll back to the previous deployment revision and confirm the pod reaches Ready.

checks: Check the deployment status and which replicas are on the old vs new revision
Check the new image tag exists in the registry and is the intended one
Check pod events for ImagePullBackOff, failed probes, or resource errors
Check the change that was deployed (diff, config, migrations)
Confirm the previous revision is still serving traffic without errors
runbooks.description: A deployment did not roll out cleanly. Stop the rollout, keep the last good version serving traffic, and inspect the failure before retrying.
runbooks.escalate_if: The previous revision is also unhealthy, or a database migration was part of the failed deploy.
runbooks.name: Failed deployment
runbooks.rollback: Roll back to the previous deployment revision; do not retry the same image until the failure is understood.

checks: Identify which backup job or restore test failed, and when it last succeeded
Check the backup job logs for the exact error (permissions, storage, timeout, corruption)
Check backup storage: capacity, permissions, and whether the backup file exists and has a plausible size
Check whether the failure is in the backup, the restore, or the test environment
Confirm no backup was deleted or overwritten after the failure
runbooks.description: A backup or a restore test failed. Treat this as serious: until a restore is proven, the backup cannot be relied on. Do not delete or overwrite any backup while investigating.
runbooks.escalate_if: Always escalate: a failed backup or restore test is a P1 until a restore is proven to work.
runbooks.name: Backup restore test failure
runbooks.rollback: There is no rollback for a failed backup. Preserve all existing backups, open an incident, and re-run the restore test only after the cause is fixed.
